title: Classic Steak Tartare with Capers, Cornichons and Egg Yolk
summary: Tender beef fillet chopped by hand and folded with a mustardy mayonnaise, capers, cornichons, shallot and herbs, shaped into rounds and topped with a golden yolk, with crisp baguette toasts on the side.
equipment: large bowl set over a bowl of ice

ingredients.item: beef fillet (tenderloin), one very fresh whole piece
ingredients.note: trimmed of all fat and silver skin

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt
extra-virgin olive oil, for the toasts

steps.title: Firm up the fillet
steps.text: Wrap the trimmed beef and give it 15 min in the freezer. Slightly firm meat holds its shape under the knife, so every cut is clean instead of squashed.

steps.title: Bake the toasts
steps.text: Heat the oven to 200 °C (180 °C fan). Brush the baguette slices with 1 tbsp oil, spread them on the tray and bake for 6-8 min until golden and crisp, then leave them to cool.

steps.title: Whisk the dressing
steps.text: Combine the mayonnaise, mustard, lemon juice, the remaining 1 tbsp oil, the salt and the pepper in the small bowl. A quick whisk gives a smooth, glossy sauce that will coat the beef evenly.

steps.title: Chop by hand
steps.text: Cut the beef into 5 mm slices, then into 5 mm strips, then across into tiny cubes; keep chopping until fine. Tip it straight into the bowl sitting over ice. A knife leaves distinct little pieces with a tender bite, where a mincer would turn it pasty.

steps.title: Fold it together
steps.text: Add the dressing, shallots, capers, cornichons, parsley and chives and fold gently with a spoon just until evenly mixed. Taste, adding more pepper if you like; overworking warms the meat and dulls the texture.

steps.title: Shape the rounds
steps.text: Set the ring on a chilled plate, spoon in a quarter of the beef and press lightly, then lift the ring away. Make a shallow dip on top with the back of a spoon and slide a yolk into it, then repeat for the other plates.

steps.title: Serve straight away
steps.text: Bring the plates to the table with the toasts while everything is still cold. Each person breaks their yolk and stirs it through the beef, where it acts as a rich, last-minute sauce.

tips: Swap the toasts for crisp potato wafers or small lettuce leaves if you prefer.
safety: RAW NOTE: the beef is eaten raw. Use a very fresh whole-muscle piece from a butcher you trust, trim and chop it yourself just before serving (never pre-minced beef), and keep it below 4 °C until it goes on the plate. Pregnant people, young children, older adults and anyone with weakened immunity should skip it.
EGG NOTE: the yolk is served raw. Use pasteurised egg yolks; pregnant people, young children, older adults and anyone with weakened immunity should leave the yolk off.
A common mistake is chopping the beef long before serving; cut and mix it in the final 15 minutes so it stays bright red and safely cold.
Wipe the knife and board between cuts and keep the bowl over ice; warmth and stray scraps are what spoil raw beef fastest.
storage: Steak tartare does not keep: serve it as soon as it is mixed and throw away any leftovers. The toasts stay crisp for 2 days in an airtight tin. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
